item.title: Ukraine fires over 1,000 drones at Russia, including hundreds launched at Moscow
item.description: Moscow's mayor described the wave of drones as the "largest ever" attack on the Russian capital and said there had been damage to a Moscow oil refinery and a residential building.
item.content:encoded:
Moscow's mayor described the wave of drones as the "largest ever" attack on the Russian capital and said there had been damage to a Moscow oil refinery and a residential building.

item.title: Saudi Arabia says Houthis tried to attack its capital
item.description: Saudi Arabia on Saturday said that Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack Riyadh with a ballistic missile, the first time the Saudi capital has been targeted since the escalation in fighting with the Iran-backed rebels opened a new front in the Iran war.
item.content:encoded:

(Image credit: Osamah Abdulrahman)

item.title: The new lines of southern Lebanon
item.description: The U.N. expanded the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon's mandate 20 years ago to include monitoring adherence to a ceasefire in fighting between Israel and Lebanon's Iran-backed Hezbollah — the militant group created in 1982 to counter a second Israeli invasion.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: France, Poland and European allies warn of escalating Russian 'hybrid' attacks
item.description: The leaders of France, Poland, and other leading European nations are alarmed over what they describe as Russian "hybrid" attacks.

item.title: Life in Kabul 5 years after the Taliban's return
item.description: Five years after the return of Taliban rule, NPR visited Kabul to see how Afghans are dealing with their new government's strict social restrictions.

item.title: Russia holds parliamentary vote in areas it seized from Ukraine in the war
item.description: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.

item.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread
item.description: Italian health authorities see evidence that rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across a wider area, during more months of the year.

item.title: U.S. and Denmark reach deal to build U.S. military presence in Greenland
item.description: President Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.

item.title: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament
item.description: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament, the Duma. It's Russia's first nationwide parliamentary race since launching its full scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

item.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
item.description: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.
